You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From db52f57211b4e45f0ebb274e2c877b211dc18591 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kajol Jain <kjain@linux.ibm.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2021 13:03:15 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Remove config check to enable bpf support for branch
 records

Branch data available to BPF programs can be very useful to get stack traces
out of userspace application.

Commit fff7b64355ea ("bpf: Add bpf_read_branch_records() helper") added BPF
support to capture branch records in x86. Enable this feature also for other
architectures as well by removing checks specific to x86.

If an architecture doesn't support branch records, bpf_read_branch_records()
still has appropriate checks and it will return an -EINVAL in that scenario.
Based on UAPI helper doc in include/uapi/linux/bpf.h, unsupported architectures
should return -ENOENT in such case. Hence, update the appropriate check to
return -ENOENT instead.

Selftest 'perf_branches' result on power9 machine which has the branch stacks
support:

 - Before this patch:

  [command]# ./test_progs -t perf_branches
   #88/1 perf_branches/perf_branches_hw:FAIL
   #88/2 perf_branches/perf_branches_no_hw:OK
   #88 perf_branches:FAIL
  Summary: 0/1 PASSED, 0 SKIPPED, 1 FAILED

 - After this patch:

  [command]# ./test_progs -t perf_branches
   #88/1 perf_branches/perf_branches_hw:OK
   #88/2 perf_branches/perf_branches_no_hw:OK
   #88 perf_branches:OK
  Summary: 1/2 PASSED, 0 SKIPPED, 0 FAILED

Selftest 'perf_branches' result on power9 machine which doesn't have branch
stack report:

 - After this patch:

  [command]# ./test_progs -t perf_branches
   #88/1 perf_branches/perf_branches_hw:SKIP
   #88/2 perf_branches/perf_branches_no_hw:OK
   #88 perf_branches:OK
  Summary: 1/1 PASSED, 1 SKIPPED, 0 FAILED

Fixes: fff7b64355eac ("bpf: Add bpf_read_branch_records() helper")
Suggested-by: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Kajol Jain <kjain@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20211206073315.77432-1-kjain@linux.ibm.com

diff --git a/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c b/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
index 25ea521fb8f1..77f13de6f9f9 100644
--- a/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
+++ b/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
@@ -1404,9 +1404,6 @@ static const struct bpf_func_proto bpf_perf_prog_read_value_proto = {
 BPF_CALL_4(bpf_read_branch_records, struct bpf_perf_event_data_kern *, ctx,
 	   void *, buf, u32, size, u64, flags)
 {
-#ifndef CONFIG_X86
-	return -ENOENT;
-#else
 	static const u32 br_entry_size = sizeof(struct perf_branch_entry);
 	struct perf_branch_stack *br_stack = ctx->data->br_stack;
 	u32 to_copy;
@@ -1415,7 +1412,7 @@ BPF_CALL_4(bpf_read_branch_records, struct bpf_perf_event_data_kern *, ctx,
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	if (unlikely(!br_stack))
-		return -EINVAL;
+		return -ENOENT;
 
 	if (flags & BPF_F_GET_BRANCH_RECORDS_SIZE)
 		return br_stack->nr * br_entry_size;
@@ -1427,7 +1424,6 @@ BPF_CALL_4(bpf_read_branch_records, struct bpf_perf_event_data_kern *, ctx,
 	memcpy(buf, br_stack->entries, to_copy);
 
 	return to_copy;
-#endif
 }
 
 static const struct bpf_func_proto bpf_read_branch_records_proto = {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c`**
   - Removed the preprocessor check for `CONFIG_X86` that restricted the `bpf_read_branch_records` function to only x86 architecture.
   - Updated the return value for the case when `br_stack` is `NULL` from `-EINVAL` to `-ENOENT`, aligning with the expected behavior for unsupported architectures.
   - The overall structure of the `bpf_read_branch_records` function remains intact, but it is now applicable to more architectures beyond just x86.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `bpf_trace.c` are aimed at broadening the support for the `bpf_read_branch_records` function to include architectures other than x86. By removing the architecture-specific checks, the function can now be utilized on systems that support branch records, while still handling unsupported architectures gracefully by returning `-ENOENT`. This change enhances the functionality of BPF programs by allowing them to access branch data across different hardware platforms, thus improving stack trace capabilities in userspace applications. The patch also addresses a previous limitation noted in commit `fff7b64355ea`, ensuring that the behavior of the function is consistent with the expectations outlined in the UAPI helper documentation.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the restriction of the `bpf_read_branch_records` function to only x86 architecture due to the presence of a preprocessor check for `CONFIG_X86`. This limitation prevented the function from being utilized on other architectures that could support branch records, leading to incorrect behavior and failure in self-tests on those systems. Additionally, the return value for unsupported architectures was incorrectly set to `-EINVAL` instead of the appropriate `-ENOENT`, which further contributed to the issue.
